objective: maximize viral growth signals — retention, sustainable views, shares and subscriber growth — while preserving originality

weak_patterns.pattern: hook_type:curiosity_claim_hook + story_format:seven_scene_story + payoff_position:mid + explanation_position:mid + script_length:short + narration_pace:natural

winning_topics: J.R.R. Tolkien: While grading monotonous student exam papers, an Oxford professor happens upon a blank page and writes an impromptu opening line about a hobbit in a hole.
Jackie Chan: The Years of Stunt Work and Background Roles Before Global Action Stardom.
Dolly Parton: Growing up in a one-room cabin with twelve siblings in the Great Smoky Mountains before becoming a global country music icon.
avoid_topics: Harland Sanders: A Failed Highway Business Led to a Global Fried Chicken Empire at Age 65.
Mary Anning: The Working-Class Woman Who Discovered Prehistoric Giants Ignored by Academia.
Boman Irani: A journey from working at a family bakery and running a photographic studio to finding major acting success in Hindi cinema at a mature age.
rules: Learn combinations, not templates; never copy winning topics literally.
Only repeated creative evidence with n>=2 is considered a proven pattern.
Use the explicit 70/20/10 creative selector for future Shorts when evidence is available.
Use one winning combination at a time so future performance remains interpretable.
Use adjacent and wild exploration to avoid creative lock-in.
Retention is primary; shares and subscriber conversion are stronger growth signals than likes.
Use actual rendered narration duration when available to learn pacing.
Reject exact repeats and near-duplicate topics before generation.
